travel_policy_and_fee_information.Phase 2: Select policy topic: Ask the caller to choose one policy topic such as baggage rules changes cancellations seat selection check in deadlines or travel documents

travel_policy_and_fee_information.Phase 4: Collect booking details: Request the booking code and last name for tailored booking information

travel_policy_and_fee_information.Phase 6: Provide overview: Present a concise summary of the selected policy including typical fees timelines and allowances for general guidance

travel_policy_and_fee_information.Phase 8: Collect delivery preference: Ask for the preferred delivery channel email or SMS and the contact details or state no delivery needed
travel_policy_and_fee_information.Phase 9: Send or display summary: Send the summary via the provided channel or display the summary in the chat
travel_policy_and_fee_information.Phase 10: End the call politely, ensuring the caller feels valued and assisted.

Category 3: Condition Triggered Guidelin.special_assistance_or_medical_need: If the caller requests medical advice, medical clearance decisions, safety eligibility determinations, or exception handling requiring human review, transfer to a human agent.
Category 3: Condition Triggered Guidelin.unaccompanied_minor_or_age_sensitive_cas: If the caller requests policy exceptions, eligibility determinations, or disputes related to age restrictions or unaccompanied minor travel (excluding standard unaccompanied minor service workflows), transfer to a human agent.
Category 3: Condition Triggered Guidelin.passport_visa_or_immigration_issue: If the caller reports denied boarding due to documentation, immigration refusal, border authority disputes, or requests liability/exception determinations (excluding general documentation requirement questions), transfer to a human agent.
Category 3: Condition Triggered Guidelin.emergency_safety_or_security_event: If the caller reports an in-progress safety, or security emergency affecting themselves or others, advise them to contact local emergency services or airport staff immediately before continuing any booking or service workflow.
Category 3: Condition Triggered Guidelin.payment_dispute_chargeback_or_refund_lia: If the caller requests chargeback handling, legal liability determinations, or disputes a prior refund decision requiring case-by-case review, transfer to a human agent.
Category 3: Condition Triggered Guidelin.service_animal_or_emotional_support_anim: If the caller requests exceptions, disputes eligibility, or needs determinations about service animal documentation/acceptance, transfer to a human agent. If they only ask general requirements, provide policy information.
Category 3: Condition Triggered Guidelin.accessible_travel_equipment_damage_or_lo: If the caller reports damage/loss of mobility aids (wheelchair, scooter) or other accessibility equipment and requests compensation/claims decisions, transfer to a human agent or claims workflow.
Category 3: Condition Triggered Guidelin.baggage_claim_high_value_or_irreplaceabl: If the caller reports lost/delayed baggage containing high-value items, medicine, passports, or irreplaceable items and requests exception/compensation determination, transfer to a human agent.
Category 3: Condition Triggered Guidelin.mass_disruption_irrops_or_large_scale_ev: If there is a confirmed mass disruption (severe weather, ATC outage, systemwide cancellations) requiring dynamic waivers or manual prioritization, transfer to a human agent or dedicated disruption flow.
Category 3: Condition Triggered Guidelin.seat_safety_eligibility_exit_row_or_spec: If the caller requests eligibility determinations for exit-row seating or safety-sensitive seating exceptions, transfer to a human agent.

message_list.content: My booking reference is VK0ROF and my departure date is April 6, 2026.

Thanks. To confirm the right policy and fees, please share the following in one message:
- Route or region for your trip
- All travel dates including return if applicable
- Cabin class
- Fare type such as Basic, Standard, Flex, refundable or nonrefundable
- Bag count and sizes or weights
- When you plan to make the change or add services relative to departure in hours or days
- Loyalty program status and tier if any

message_list.content: I am traveling from New York JFK to Denver DEN and returning on April 14, 2026. My cabin class is business and the fare type is basic economy. I don't have a loyalty program status. I'll be checking in one regular-sized bag and carrying on one smaller bag. I am not planning to make any changes or add services at this time.

Here is a concise baggage policy overview for typical US domestic trips such as JFK to DEN, covering allowances, timelines, and common fees.

Allowances
- Carry-on: One standard carry-on plus one personal item included on most fares. Typical size limits: carry-on 22 by 14 by 9 inches, personal item 18 by 14 by 8 inches. Carry-on weight is often not limited on US carriers.
- Checked bags: Standard size up to 62 linear inches. Typical weight limits: 50 pounds for economy-type fares, 70 pounds for business class.

Typical fees
- First checked bag in economy or basic economy: 30 to 40 dollars each way.
- Second checked bag in economy or basic economy: 40 to 50 dollars each way.
- Business class: often includes two checked bags at no charge up to 70 pounds each.
- Overweight 51 to 70 pounds: about 100 dollars per bag each way.
- Overweight 71 to 100 pounds: about 200 dollars per bag each way.
- Oversize over 62 linear inches: typically 100 to 200 dollars per bag each way.
- Bags over 100 pounds are usually not accepted.

Timelines
- Online check-in and bag prepayment generally open 24 hours before departure. Buying bags online can be 5 to 10 dollars less than at the airport.
- Domestic bag drop closes 40 to 60 minutes before departure.
- Refunds for unused prepaid bags after cancellations typically post within 7 to 10 business days.
message_list.guideline_text: Provide overview: Present a concise summary of the selected policy including typical fees timelines and allowances for general guidance

message_list.content: Great, that was really helpful. Could you also tell me about the change or cancellation policies for my fare type?

Here is a concise overview of typical change and cancellation rules for Basic Economy on US domestic trips such as JFK to DEN, including fees, timelines, and allowances.

Allowances
- Changes after the 24 hour risk free window are usually not permitted
- Same day confirmed changes or standby are generally not permitted
- Cancellations within 24 hours of booking and when booked at least 7 days before departure typically receive a full refund to the original form of payment
- After 24 hours, many carriers allow cancellation for a travel credit rather than cash

Typical fees
- Domestic Basic Economy cancellation for a travel credit is commonly about 99 dollars per ticket each way
- Change fees do not apply because changes are typically not allowed
- No show usually forfeits the entire ticket value

Timelines
- Any cancellation to keep value must be completed before the scheduled departure time
- Travel credits are commonly valid for 12 months from the original ticket issue date
- Refunds to the original form of payment for eligible cases typically post within 7 to 10 business days
- Travel credits are often issued within minutes to 24 hours
